problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=R\times [-1,1]$ in the Cartesian plane?
worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set

$$
S=R\times [-1,1]
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is any real number and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-1,1].$

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in R,\,y\in [-1,1]}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{0}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $0$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-1,1].$

$$
{S}_{0}={(0,y)\,:\,y\in [-1,1]}
$$

We can represent ${S}_{0}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/588f2574b1aaf0e96895816ca34bd9c6900a9b13342f44bd4104ad2bf4270bf5.png)

Now, consider a general ${S}_{i}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals some $i\in R$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-1,1].$

$$
{S}_{i}={(i,y)\,:\,y\in [-1,1]}
$$

For each $i\in R,$ ${S}_{i}$ is a vertical line segment from the point $(i,-1)$ to the point $(i,1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/8458978c2766d899b03149de53739650932875d6463c25dd3bbde99bc6a71ea7.png)

Our Cartesian product $S$ is the union of these subsets over $R:$

$$
S={⋃}_{i\in R}{S}_{i}.
$$

As $i$ runs over $R,$ these line segments sweep the following bar that represents the union ${⋃}_{i\in R}{S}_{i}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/6fc81e487503ce86d3bf5366e57db087484e8bd1e8bafd52738c65e8e173c387.png)
